name: Single Digital Gateway Regulation
evidence_rating: moderate on usage, thin on impact: usage and satisfaction indicators measured by the Commission; forecast cost savings unmeasured; no independent impact studies found
summary: The Single Digital Gateway promised to save businesses EUR 11-55 billion a year by putting EU and national information and procedures online. The Commission's 2023 report shows the Your Europe portal is heavily used (43 million visits in 2022) with over 90% satisfaction, but only about half of key procedures could be completed online by users from other EU countries. The promised savings have not been measured, and the 2025 evaluation was not found.

indicators.indicator: Share of users who found the information they were looking for
indicators.evidence: Your Europe user survey: 77% of businesses and 76% of citizens found what they were looking for (2023 report).
Your Europe ~43 million visits in 2022 (third most visited Commission site); national SDG pages >100 million visits a year in 2021-2022.
92.5% of citizens and 90.3% of businesses rated the portal satisfactory or better; assistance services 4.3/5 average from ~3,200 feedbacks (self-selected respondents).

indicators.objective: Core procedures online for cross-border users
indicators.indicator: Share of (cross-border) users able to complete procedures fully online
indicators.evidence: eGovernment Benchmark (preliminary, 2023): SDG procedures 84% completable online by nationals but only 47% by cross-border users; Once-Only Technical System still being rolled out.

indicators.indicator: Annual cost savings for businesses expanding cross-border
indicators.evidence: Not measured; the Commission's only ex-post figure is about EUR 2.5m a year in avoided legal-advice costs for Your Europe business users.

literature.citation: European Commission (2017), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on establishing a single digital gateway (executive summary), SWD(2017) 214 (full IA SWD(2017) 213)
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on establishing a single digital gateway (executive summary)
literature.outcomes: administrative burden; cross-border trade; public costs
literature.headline: Could reduce business costs by EUR 11-55bn a year (based on 9 procedures and 9 information topics); set-up cost about EUR 5.8m per Member State, EUR 4.3-4.8m for the Commission
literature.summary_plain: The Commission estimated that a single EU portal for information and online procedures could save businesses EUR 11-55 billion a year.

literature.citation: European Commission (2023), First Implementation Report on the Single Digital Gateway, COM(2023) 534
literature.title: First Implementation Report on the Single Digital Gateway
literature.method: monitoring report (usage statistics, user surveys, eGovernment Benchmark)
literature.headline: 43m Your Europe visits in 2022; 90%+ satisfaction; 76-77% found information; 6.5m assistance cases 2021-22; SDG procedures 84% online for nationals vs 47% for cross-border users; ~EUR 2.5m/yr saved in legal advice
literature.summary_plain: The first implementation report shows heavy use and high satisfaction with the Your Europe portal, but fewer than half of key procedures could yet be completed online by people from other EU countries.
literature.quality: Commission self-assessment; usage data robust, savings minimal

literature.citation: Graux (2021), The Single Digital Gateway Regulation as an Enabler and Constraint of Once-Only in Europe, in The Once-Only Principle, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 12621, Springer
literature.title: The Single Digital Gateway Regulation as an Enabler and Constraint of Once-Only in Europe
literature.venue: in The Once-Only Principle, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 12621, Springer
literature.headline: Analyses how the Regulation enables the once-only principle for cross-border procedures while its design constrains its scope
literature.summary_plain: A legal analysis argues the Regulation both pushes forward and limits the 'tell us once' idea for cross-border paperwork.

literature.authors: Sofie Voigt, Alinka Rother, Liadán Sage (ÖFIT, Fraunhofer FOKUS)
literature.title: The Single Digital Gateway Regulation - Lessons from Implementation in Five EU Countries
literature.method: structured qualitative assessment: interviews with twelve experts from Germany, Austria, Ireland, Spain and Sweden
literature.outcomes: implementation status, organisational challenges in national SDGR rollout
literature.headline: No EU Member State fully implemented the Single Digital Gateway Regulation by the end-2023 deadline; interviewees cite unclear interpretation, weak coordination and limited resources.
literature.summary_plain: Researchers interviewed officials in five countries and found that none had fully delivered the EU's one-stop online portal rules on time, mainly because of coordination and resource problems.
literature.quality: Qualitative, 12 interviews, no quantitative outcome measure; publicly funded German research centre.
literature.interested_party: publicly funded (German federal ministry-backed Fraunhofer centre)
literature.citation: Sofie Voigt, Alinka Rother, Liadán Sage (ÖFIT, Fraunhofer FOKUS) (2024), The Single Digital Gateway Regulation - Lessons from Implementation in Five EU Countries, Kompetenzzentrum Öffentliche IT (ÖFIT) white paper

literature.title: eGovernment Benchmark 2025
literature.method: mystery-shopper measurement of 14,104 government websites across EU27, nine life events, 20 indicators (Nov 2024), with new SDGR compliance indicators
literature.outcomes: online availability of SDGR procedures, cross-border vs national service quality, OOTS availability
literature.headline: 93% of Single Digital Gateway procedures are available online, but cross-border users benefit less than national users and the Once-Only Technical System was not yet available.
literature.summary_plain: A large check of EU government websites found almost all the procedures the gateway rules require are now online, but people from other EU countries still get a worse service and automatic document sharing between countries is not working yet.
literature.quality: Large systematic measurement, descriptive; only the publisher's press release read, not the full report.
literature.interested_party: consultancy contractor for the European Commission
literature.citation: Capgemini et al. (2025), eGovernment Benchmark 2025, eGovernment Benchmark (annual European Commission study)
